# Rohit Malekar

> Research, essays, and selected work on Ethereum in institutional finance, coordination and public goods, product craft, and living well.

Rohit Malekar writes and thinks in public at rohitmalekar.in. This site is a digital garden — essays compound from atomic notes over time. Rohit researches how banks, market infrastructure and regulators in India, Singapore and Hong Kong could use Ethereum for tokenisation, settlement and verification. He writes The Monsoon Ledger (https://themonsoonledger.com/), a weekly on policy, regulation and Ethereum across Asian finance, and was lead researcher on Ethereum and Indian Institutional Finance (https://institutions.ethindia.co/briefing.html) for ETHIndia. Before this he spent four years designing grant programs and building analytics inside Ethereum, and twenty years in strategy and analytics at Deloitte and Medallia.

## About & working together

- [About](https://rohitmalekar.in/about): Who Rohit is: twenty years across consulting, product, and research (Deloitte, Medallia), four years allocating capital inside Ethereum, now researching Ethereum adoption in Asian institutional finance. Includes ready-to-use speaker bios.
- [Work With Me](https://rohitmalekar.in/work-with-me): Full-time roles, advisory, commissioned research, and speaking on Ethereum adoption in institutional finance across India, Singapore and Hong Kong.
- [CV](https://rohitmalekar.in/cv): Full professional chronology with roles and dates — institutional finance research since 2026 (ETHIndia, The Monsoon Ledger), independent practice 2023-2026 (Gitcoin, Metagov, Open Source Observer, Scroll), preceded by Deloitte Digital, Medallia, Deloitte Consulting, and Tech Mahindra.

## Writings

Essays organized into five themes:

- [Ethereum & Institutional Finance](https://rohitmalekar.in/articles/institutions/): Privacy, settlement, and what it takes for regulated institutions to adopt public blockchains.
- [Public Goods & Coordination](https://rohitmalekar.in/articles/coordination/): Funding mechanisms, grants programs, DAOs, and the data behind making Web3 ecosystems work.
- [The Art of Work](https://rohitmalekar.in/articles/art-of-work/): Careers, product craft, consulting lessons, and staying competent in the age of AI.
- [Building Better Orgs](https://rohitmalekar.in/articles/building-better-orgs/): Work culture, leadership, and how organizations actually decide.
- [Living Well](https://rohitmalekar.in/articles/living-well/): Attention, contentment, health, and the slow compounding of a deliberate life.

## Featured essays

- [Being Right Isn't Enough — Lessons for Ethereum from a 90s OS War](https://rohitmalekar.in/being-right-ethereum): GNU Hurd was architecturally superior to Linux and lost anyway. The same pattern haunts Ethereum — five lessons.
- [WTF is Cluster-Matching QF?](https://rohitmalekar.in/cluster-matching-qf): How quadratic funding breaks under collusion, and a mechanism that fixes it.
- [Grants for Public Good — A Roadmap for Resilient Democratic Funding](https://rohitmalekar.in/grants-for-public-good): A roadmap for funding that survives its funders.
- [Harnessing Nature's Wisdom for Mechanism Design](https://rohitmalekar.in/harnessing-natures-wisdom): What ecosystems already know about incentives.
- [The Infrastructure for Insight — Cultivating Personal Judgement in the Age of Generation](https://rohitmalekar.in/pkm): Building a personal knowledge system when anyone can generate plausible content.
- [Why Most Organisations Aren't Ready for AI (and It's Not a Tech Problem)](https://rohitmalekar.in/ai-readiness): The real blockers to AI adoption are organizational, not technical.
- [The Biggest Risk With AI Isn't Job Loss. It's Loss of Agency](https://rohitmalekar.in/ai-agency-loss): Why agency, not employment, is the thing to protect.
- [AI as Amplifier — Three Shifts That Change How You Work](https://rohitmalekar.in/ai-as-amplifier): Three concrete shifts for working well alongside AI.
- [If You Aren't Content Without it, You Won't be Content With it](https://rohitmalekar.in/contentment): On contentment, ambition, and the things we chase.
- [Consistency Compounds — Insights from 6 Years of Cycling Data](https://rohitmalekar.in/consistency): What six years of personal cycling data reveals about consistency.

## Notes

- [Notes](https://rohitmalekar.in/notes/): Atomic notes library — short reflections and referenced ideas that compound into essays over time.
- [Reflections](https://rohitmalekar.in/notes/self/): First-person syntheses worked out in Rohit's own words.
- [Reference Notes](https://rohitmalekar.in/notes/reference/): Ideas from books, papers, and talks, each with its source cited.

## Portfolio

- [Portfolio](https://rohitmalekar.in/portfolio/): Selected work across research, data tools, writing, and speaking — funding systems and analytics for digital public goods, including work with Gitcoin, Octant, and across the Ethereum ecosystem.
- [Case study: ENS DAO Governance Research Platform](https://rohitmalekar.in/ens-governance-analytics): Reproducible analytics stack (Dagster, dbt, DuckDB) across 7 onchain and forum data sources behind Metagov's independent governance retrospective of ENS DAO — cited in decisions over a $400M+ treasury.
- [Case study: GG24 Interop Round](https://rohitmalekar.in/gg24-interop-case-study): Designing and operating Ethereum's first interop-focused grants domain — a $100K+ quadratic funding round — and what the data showed about QF underfunding infrastructure.

## Off the Track

- [Off the Track](https://rohitmalekar.in/off-the-track/): Long-distance cycling around Bangalore and poetry — the slow miles and metaphors behind the rest of the work.
